context: Request: the largest settlement the firm has reached, counting each at the amount its executed agreement defines (for a pitch). Rubric: 1021-00006 (Verimark Hospitality v. Coastal Palms, $87,500,000 Settlement Amount; $25M is only its initial payment) as the answer, its figure, and a precision criterion. 1021-00003 (Verimark v. insurers, $47.3M) and 1027-00003 ($52.85M redemption price) are not the answer.

runs.failure_point: It never opened the needed matter: its own skipped line ranges credited that matter's amount to a sibling matter of the same client, and the sibling's smaller amount became the answer.

first_error.stage: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
first_error.why: The needed matter's executed agreement and its amount appeared in the scan output at [39]-[41], but the agent's own skipped line ranges put that amount under a sibling matter's header, so it opened only the sibling's agreement (which stated a smaller amount) and never opened the needed matter.
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The scan review at [43] said lines 151-183 of the printed output were skipped and asked to check them; the agent went straight to reading the sibling matter, which the same review had named as the top candidate.

runs.failure_point: It read the needed matter's initial payment from scan snippets as its settlement amount and never opened the executed agreement, so a redemption price in another matter became the largest.

first_error.why: The answer lists the needed matter at its initial-payment figure, not the larger settlement amount its executed agreement defines; the agent took that figure from scan snippets (evidence seen at [42]-[46], summary at [49]) and never opened the agreement, so another matter's redemption price became the largest.
first_error.critic_note: The scan review at [50] described the needed matter's hits as drafts and redlines and told the agent to open the two other candidates' agreements; it did so and never returned to the needed matter. Later reviews did not name the figure.

divergence: Mixed (T1 passes; T0, T2 fail). All runs surfaced the needed matter's execution-version agreement through path searches and text scans. They split at the scan stage that read amounts from snippets: T1 ran a sweep for defined settlement terms that printed amounts sorted by size, then read that agreement and wrote it. T0 printed chosen line ranges of its scan output, skipping the needed matter's header lines, so the larger figure was credited to a sibling matter; T2 took the needed matter's initial payment as its amount. Neither opened the needed matter's agreement. The critic differed: in T0 the scan review flagged the skipped line ranges (ignored), in T2 the scan review called the needed matter's hits drafts and pointed to two other matters, and in T1 the reviews only flagged path filters as possibly incomplete.
